interactions.summary: Students test Jiang's model by recasting homosexuality as a secret-society mechanism with hierarchy, then question whether the same logic still holds under modern openness and acceptance.

Jiang updates the argument from medieval text to contemporary politics, claiming decadent elites no longer hide corruption, that family-centered restraint has collapsed, and that modern identity variants follow the same self-indulgent logic in Dante's terms.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Jiang answer with student follow-up question

claims.claim: Jiang says the intention of homosexual networks is not evil in itself; persecution drives them into secret-society behavior that can then solidify into hierarchy and institutional infiltration.
He argues that once a society becomes decadent, elites cease caring about family or social reproduction and instead openly indulge desire without responsibility to the broader society.
Jiang uses Donald Trump and a hypothetical Democratic return in 2028 to argue that rival elites will intensify corruption rather than restore republican virtue.
claims.temporal_scope: Prediction and diagnosis made on 2026-06-24 about 2028 U.S. politics.

claims.claim: He says earlier societies at least required elites to honor family publicly, whereas current openness can coincide with a deeper indifference to society's long-term health.

signature_moments.moment: Corruption is no longer masked: the elite no longer bother pretending, and the next faction will arrive only to loot more efficiently.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It turns the Dante discussion into a live U.S. regime-diagnosis and explicit forecast.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang grudgingly credits old hypocrisy as a sign that family still had to be honored in public, even when elites violated it privately.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It captures his paradoxical view that open vice may mark deeper civic decay than concealed vice.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: The stage at which elites stop orienting themselves around family and society and instead organize politics around self-indulgence and open corruption.

chronology_notes.note: On 2026-06-24 Jiang predicts that a post-Trump Democratic return in 2028 would deepen rather than clean up U.S. corruption.

uncertainty_notes.note: Segment 0037 contains several ASR glitches, but the through-line about decadence, family, and elite self-indulgence is still clear.
